content.text: Found two real bugs: a class-name collision (`.cands`/`.steps` matched both spacers and sections, killing their flex-grow) and a flex-grow value below 1, which makes Chromium scale down the distributed free space so the photo never absorbed the surplus. Fixing both.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p='flyer.html'; s=open(p).read()
# rename spacer modifier classes so they can never collide with section classes
for old,new in [('sp top','gap gap-top'),('sp hero','gap gap-hero'),('sp cands','gap gap-cands'),
                ('sp cta','gap gap-cta'),('sp steps','gap gap-steps'),('sp foot','gap gap-foot'),
                ('sp bottom','gap gap-bottom')]:
    s=s.replace('class="%s"'%old,'class="%s"'%new)
s=s.replace('.sp{','.gap{')
for old,new in [('.sp.top','.gap-top'),('.sp.hero','.gap-hero'),('.sp.cands','.gap-cands'),
                ('.sp.cta','.gap-cta'),('.sp.steps','.gap-steps'),('.sp.foot','.gap-foot'),
                ('.sp.bottom','.gap-bottom')]:
    s=s.replace(old+'   {',new+'{').replace(old+'  {',new+'{').replace(old+' {',new+'{').replace(old+'{',new+'{')
s=s.replace('flex:0.0001 1 auto;','flex:1 1 auto;')
open(p,'w').write(s)
print(re.search(r'\.gap\{.*?\.gap-bottom\{[^}]*\}', s, re.S).group(0))
print('---- classes in markup:', re.findall(r'class="gap[^"]*"', s))
EOF

content.text:
Done. All three PNGs are rendered at exact pixel sizes.

**Files:** `portrait.png` (1080×1350), `wide.png` (1200×1000), `sky.png` (300×600), built from `flyer.html` via `build.sh` (which stamps the scale into `portrait/wide/sky.html` and runs the `playwright screenshot` command you specified).

**How scaling works:** one document drives all three sizes. Every content dimension — type, icons, avatars, padding, gaps — is `calc(Npx * var(--s))` with `--s` set to `1`, `0.85`, `0.28`. Bands (`width:100%`) and the column flexbox stay layout-driven, so they fill the canvas at any width while the content inside scales.

**Defects found and fixed during checking:**
1. **Class-name collision** — `.cands` and `.steps` matched both the spacer divs and the content sections, so the later section rule (`flex:0 0 auto`) overrode those spacers' `flex-grow` and froze them at minimum height. This produced a lopsided rhythm in portrait (32px gap next to a 71px gap). Spacers renamed to `.gap-*`.
2. **`flex-grow` below 1** — I'd given the photo band `flex-grow:0.0001` to make it a last-resort absorber, but CSS scales distributed free space by the grow sum when it's under 1, so the band absorbed nothing and sky ended up with 216px of dead space under the footer. Set to `1`; the spacers' large grow factors keep portrait/wide photos effectively unchanged (+2px) while sky's surplus flows to the band.
3. **Sky's vertical rhythm** — the 1:2 canvas has more slack than the entire scaled content, so gaps were stretching to 4.85× their master value (vs 1.8× in portrait), making sections float apart. Gaps now cap at 3.6× their master size and the photo band takes the remainder, cropping taller (207px) instead.
4. **Line-box clipping** — headline (`line-height:1.04`) and the CTA label (`line-height:1`) had content taller than their own boxes; loosened to 1.1 / 1.16.

**Verified via DOM measurement at all three sizes:** nothing outside the viewport, no section overlap, both bands span edge-to-edge (0→W), column centres evenly spaced (portrait 332.66/332.67, wide 376.77/376.77, sky 92.35/92.35), and the photo keeps `object-fit:cover` at every band aspect so it crops rather than distorts. I also inspected 4× zoomed crops of the sky to confirm the small type and SVG icons stay crisp and complete.

One note: the sky's photo band is 207px rather than a literal 0.28× of the master's 296px. That's deliberate — the surplus height had to go somewhere, and letting the full-bleed band crop taller reads better than pushing the sections apart. All actual content (type, icons, spacing, column widths) is exactly 0.28×. If you'd prefer the band held to a strict 83px with the slack in the gaps instead, raise `--gmax` in `flyer.html` and rebuild.
